title: Do Cryptocurrency Markets Differentiate Infrastructure from Regulatory Shocks? A Multi-Moment Event Study with Dependence-Robust Inference
abstract: arXiv:2602.07046v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Do cryptocurrency markets respond differently to infrastructure and regulatory shocks? We study returns and conditional variance on a shared sample of 50 events and six assets (January 2019--August 2025), using GJR-GARCH-X models and dependence-aware inference. Treating event inclusion as a design parameter, we trace the variance differential across inclusion screens. Curated high-salience events yield a $3.49\times$ point-estimate multiplier, whereas a mechanical impact filter on a broad reconstructed candidate pool yields approximately $0.5$--$1.6\times$. This pattern is descriptive and selection-conditional, not an inferential comparison between screens. The curated variance differential is not significant against its fitted sharp per-asset-equality null under the conditional fixed-path Student-$t$-copula bootstrap ($p\approx0.39$). Floored recursive sensitivity gives one-sided $p=0.025$ at baseline and $0.041$ with asset-specific

translated_title: 加密货币市场能否区分基础设施冲击与监管冲击？一项基于依赖稳健推断的多矩事件研究
translated_abstract: 加密货币市场对基础设施冲击和监管冲击的反应是否存在差异？我们在一个包含50个事件和六种资产的共同样本（2019年1月至2025年8月）上研究收益率和条件方差，采用GJR-GARCH-X模型和依赖感知推断方法。我们将事件纳入视为一个设计参数，追踪了不同纳入筛选标准下的方差差异。精心筛选的高显著性事件产生了3.49倍的点估计乘数，而在广泛重建的候选事件池上应用机械影响筛选则产生约0.5至1.6倍的乘数。需要指出的是，这一模式是描述性的且以选择为条件，并非筛选方法之间的推断性比较。在条件固定路径Student-t-copula bootstrap检验下，精心筛选组相对于其拟合的严格逐资产相等零假设的方差差异并不显著（p≈0.39）。下限递归敏感性分析在基线设定下给出单侧p=0.025，在逐资产设定下为0.041。
tldr: 该研究利用GJR-GARCH-X模型和依赖稳健推断，在50个事件和六种资产上检验加密货币市场对基础设施与监管冲击的差异化反应，发现高显著性事件组的方差乘数（3.49倍）虽远高于机械筛选组（0.5至1.6倍），但统计上并不显著，表明这一差异更多源于事件选择方式而非市场本身的差异化定价。
en_tdlr: Using GJR-GARCH-X models and dependence-robust inference across 50 events and six assets (2019–2025), this study finds that while curated high-salience events yield a 3.49× variance multiplier versus 0.5–1.6× under mechanical impact filters, the differential is statistically insignificant, indicating that event selection rather than market differentiation drives the observed pattern.
